Central configuration policy for bounded-channel pipelines. Provides consistent backpressure settings across the application. Use static presets for common scenarios: Default - General-purpose event pipelines (100k capacity, DropOldest) HighThroughput - Streaming data pipelines (50k capacity, DropOldest) DurableStreaming - Persistence-critical streaming pipelines (50k capacity, Wait) MessageBuffer - Internal message buffering (50k capacity, DropOldest, no metrics) MaintenanceQueue - Background tasks (100 capacity, Wait/backpressure) Logging - Log channels (1k capacity, DropOldest) CompletionQueue - Completion notifications (500 capacity, Wait/backpressure)

## CircuitBreaker

Qualified name: <code>Meridian.Core.Resilience.CircuitBreaker</code>. Kind: `class`.

Source: [src/Meridian.Core/Resilience/CircuitBreaker.cs:40](../../../../src/Meridian.Core/Resilience/CircuitBreaker.cs#L40).

Canonical consecutive-failure circuit breaker shared by the hand-rolled resilience sites (subscription auto-resubscribe, composite sink fan-out). One state machine: Closed → (threshold consecutive failures) → Open → (break elapses) → HalfOpen → success closes / failure re-opens. The clock is injectable so call sites remain deterministic under test, and the StateChanged hook lets each site keep emitting its own metrics at the exact transition points it always had.

Lightweight cron expression parser supporting five-field POSIX cron plus the explicit d#n ordinal-day extension and a lone L (last day of month) in the day-of-month field. Format: minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week Examples: &quot;0 2 * * *&quot; - Daily at 2:00 AM &quot;0 3 * * 0&quot; - Every Sunday at 3:00 AM &quot;0 1 * * 0#1&quot; - First Sunday of each month at 1:00 AM &quot;30 6 * * 1-5&quot; - Weekdays at 6:30 AM &quot;0 0 1 * *&quot; - First day of each month at midnight &quot;0 8 L * *&quot; - Last day of each month at 8:00 AM &quot;*/15 * * * *&quot; - Every 15 minutes
